summary.intent: Take the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' hackathon challenge for Soony: analyze the confidential data drops, then build an agent product that rechecks the launch plan against documents, flags contradictions and acts on suppliers with human approval, generalizing beyond Soony.
summary.outcome: Found that the Collector's Edition misses Sunday (art books overbooked by 72,000, 5,600 failed statues, game card shortfall). Built a Python/FastAPI + web app with a polling store, extraction/papercheck, decision cards, email review, duplicate-send guard, routines UI and drop-rehearsal fixes, committed on jonas/today-flow. Still unpushed, and the 12:00 hand-in (README, demo script, video) isn't done.

repo: Portal API has only GET /api/v1/files, /files/{path} and /archive.zip. There are no webhooks or notifications, so new drops are found by polling the file list and comparing SHA-256; files can be replaced under the same name.
Data and notes live in gitignored data/. .env holds SOONY_PORTAL_TOKEN and is gitignored; .env.example is committed.

The team shares one mailbox. The app only knew about its own sends, so manual emails and Lucas's Pulse console (origin/new-approach, pulse-console/server.mjs) bypassed it. This caused a double art-book order and stray emails to Hwaseong. Fixed by reading the sent folder (outbox.py) and adding a 409 duplicate guard on approve.

Drop drill on a copy of state exposed that a renamed CSV column silently auto-closed real cards, that two modules wrote the same impacts file and crashed the pipeline, that any address in a supplier JSON profile was trusted as a send target, and that the oldest tracker version won.
Teammate workflow lives in CLAUDE.md and PROGRESS.md; tasks are claimed with a Now line.
Entire only writes a checkpoint when repo files change, so sessions that only read files show 'no files modified, skipping checkpoint'.
Replies to side or tracking emails must not mark a case as sent; they add info only.

code.finding: Routine diagram rewritten into When, Only if (numbered AND list with funnel counts) and Then groups; user now wants n8n-style node cards, with one Only-if node.
Counts matching cases per condition in the browser, mirroring routines.py. Waiting and replies triggers are approximate.
Reads the shared mailbox sent folder and assigns emails to cases by thread reference, then supplier plus PO, then unique part number.
Compares newer JSON supplier profiles against profile.csv. A new contact is not a send target until confirmed. Commit b0cff82 originally lacked this file, so it wouldn't start.

workflow: Subagents suit bulk cross-checks (200 order confirmations plus 59 scans), drop drills on copies, and UX reviews. Verify their output and commit it in topic-sized commits.
An agent's broad `git commit` can sweep in another worker's uncommitted edits, as happened with b0cff82. Check the working tree and run tests before committing.
Do not run drills against the real mailbox or state; use copies with ASK_REPLY_POLL=off, ASK_TEAMS=off and ASK_LLM_PROVIDER=none.
Screenshots (desktop and phone) after each UI change caught wording and layout bugs such as the stray period and the unnumbered chosen option.
Keep confidential portal data out of code and external services; findings go in gitignored notes.

friction: The portal token was initially empty, so the API returned 401 and blocked all analysis until it was supplied.
Teammate Lucas's Pulse console sent unvetted emails through the shared mailbox, including three confusing ones to Hwaseong and one to an external Gmail address (it bounced).
A manual order from the shared mailbox at 07:04 duplicated the app's 06:50 order, and the app didn't see it.
My commit b0cff82 accidentally included api.py changes without the new supplier_master.py file, so that commit alone wouldn't start.
My manual tracking-question replies wrongly closed three cards (clear cases, statues, Boise), so they had to be reopened.
UI bugs: an awkward claim sentence with a stray period, an unnumbered chosen option, and the case list not scrolling with J/K navigation.
The app's sign-off rule sends every costed case to Maren, stricter than the approval policy (€16,800 is within the buyer limit).
Some UX steps and the 'confirmed orders as inbound' builder were still running when the transcript ended.
